facts.raw_span: A 75-year-old Caucasian woman was admitted with a prosthetic hip infection 10 days after revision surgery
hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and folate deficiency
pulse 80/min, respiratory rate 24/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air
Sodium 142 mmol/L, potassium 3.5 mmol/L, chloride 118 mmol/L, bicarbonate 5 mmol/L
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.18, pCO2 1.7 kPa, pO2 16.7 kPa, bicarbonate 8.3 mmol/L, base excess –22.7 mmol/L

concepts.why: The patient has a history of chronic kidney disease and is presenting with metabolic acidosis, which is a common complication of CKD.

support_spans: A 75-year-old Caucasian woman was admitted with a prosthetic hip infection 10 days after revision surgery
drowsiness, confusion, disorientation, and hyperventilation
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.18, pCO2 1.7 kPa, pO2 16.7 kPa, bicarbonate 8.3 mmol/L, base excess –22.7 mmol/L
concepts.why: The patient is presenting with symptoms consistent with septic shock, including hyperventilation and altered mental status, in the context of a prosthetic hip infection.
The patient's Glasgow Coma Scale score of 12 and severe metabolic acidosis with a high anion gap and low bicarbonate level, along with hyperventilation, suggest a complex acid-base disturbance.
